\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{વળાંક} (vaḷā̃k)}{વળાંક (vaḷā̃k)}]{\gu{વળાંક} (vaḷā̃k) — a bend (in a road)}

\label{lesson:GU-C295-valak}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for a slope, then the Gujarati for consciousness.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{વળાંક}}
\textbf{\gu{વળાંક}} — \emph{vaḷā̃k} — \textquotedblleft{}a bend (in a road)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{વળાંક} \gu{પર} \gu{ગાડી} \gu{ખૂબ} \gu{ઝડપી} \gu{હતી}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{vaḷā̃k par gāḍī khūb jhaḍpī hatī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The car was going very fast on the bend.
\end{quote}

A masculine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{વળાંક}} (\emph{vaḷā̃k}) is built on \textbf{\gu{વળવું}}, to turn, from Sanskrit \emph{válati}, \textquotedblleft{}turns\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 11405), with the ending \emph{-āṅk}: the place where a road turns. \textbf{\gu{વળાંક} \gu{પર} \gu{ધીમે} \gu{ચલાવો}}, drive slowly on the bend.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vaḷā̃k}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vaḷā̃k}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vaḷā̃k par gāḍī khūb jhaḍpī hatī.} — The car was going very fast on the bend.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for a slope, then the Gujarati for consciousness, then say \emph{vaḷā̃k} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{વળાંક} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A bend (in a road)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{બ્રેક} (brek)}{બ્રેક (brek)}]{\gu{બ્રેક} (brek) — a brake}

\label{lesson:GU-C295-brek}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for consciousness, then the Gujarati for a bend.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{બ્રેક}}
\textbf{\gu{બ્રેક}} — \emph{brek} — \textquotedblleft{}a brake\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{ડ્રાઈવરે} \gu{છેલ્લી} \gu{પળે} \gu{બ્રેક} \gu{મારી}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ḍrāīvre chellī paḷe brek mārī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The driver braked at the last moment.
\end{quote}

A feminine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{બ્રેક}} (\emph{brek}) is borrowed from English \emph{brake}, taken in as a feminine noun. A driver \textbf{\gu{બ્રેક} \gu{મારે} \gu{છે}}, slams on the brakes.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{brek}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{brek}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḍrāīvre chellī paḷe brek mārī.} — The driver braked at the last moment.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for consciousness, then the Gujarati for a bend, then say \emph{brek} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{બેદરકાર} (bedarkār)}{બેદરકાર (bedarkār)}]{\gu{બેદરકાર} (bedarkār) — careless}

\label{lesson:GU-C295-bedarkar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for a bend, then the Gujarati for a brake.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{બેદરકાર}}
\textbf{\gu{બેદરકાર}} — \emph{bedarkār} — \textquotedblleft{}careless\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{બેદરકાર} \gu{ડ્રાઈવરને} \gu{લીધે} \gu{આ} \gu{અકસ્માત} \gu{થયો}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bedarkār ḍrāīvarne līdhe ā akasmāt thayo.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This accident happened because of a careless driver.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{બેદરકાર}} (\emph{bedarkār}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{bē-}, \textquotedblleft{}without\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{darkār}, \textquotedblleft{}needed, wanted\textquotedblright{}: someone who does not care what is needed. \textbf{\gu{બેદરકાર} \gu{ડ્રાઈવર}}, a careless driver.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bedarkār}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bedarkār}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bedarkār ḍrāīvarne līdhe ā akasmāt thayo.} — This accident happened because of a careless driver.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for a bend, then the Gujarati for a brake, then say \emph{bedarkār} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{દંડ} (danḍ)}{દંડ (danḍ)}]{\gu{દંડ} (danḍ) — a fine (penalty)}

\label{lesson:GU-C295-dand}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for a brake, then the Gujarati for careless.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{દંડ}}
\textbf{\gu{દંડ}} — \emph{danḍ} — \textquotedblleft{}a fine (penalty)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{પોલીસે} \gu{ડ્રાઈવરને} \gu{હજાર} \gu{રૂપિયાનો} \gu{દંડ} \gu{કર્યો}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{polīse ḍrāīvarne hajār rūpiyāno danḍ karyo.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police fined the driver a thousand rupees.
\end{quote}

A masculine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{દંડ}} (\emph{danḍ}) is a tatsama, Sanskrit \emph{daṇḍa}, \textquotedblleft{}a stick, a rod\textquotedblright{}, the rod of punishment; its verb \emph{daṇḍáyati} means \textquotedblleft{}chastises, fines\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 6136). A fine is made with \textbf{\gu{કરવું}}: \textbf{\gu{દંડ} \gu{કર્યો}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{danḍ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{danḍ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{polīse ḍrāīvarne hajār rūpiyāno danḍ karyo.} — The police fined the driver a thousand rupees.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for a brake, then the Gujarati for careless, then say \emph{danḍ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{દંડ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A fine (penalty)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{કચડવું} (kacaḍvũ)}{કચડવું (kacaḍvũ)}]{\gu{કચડવું} (kacaḍvũ) — to crush; to run over}

\label{lesson:GU-C295-kacadvu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for careless, then the Gujarati for a fine.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{કચડવું}}
\textbf{\gu{કચડવું}} — \emph{kacaḍvũ} — \textquotedblleft{}to crush; to run over\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{ગાડીએ} \gu{રસ્તા} \gu{પર} \gu{એક} \gu{કૂતરાને} \gu{કચડી} \gu{નાખ્યો}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{gāḍīe rastā par ek kūtrāne kacḍī nākhyo.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The car ran over a dog on the road.
\end{quote}

Past, with \gu{તેણે} (he or she …): \gu{તેણે} \gu{કીડી} \gu{કચડી}, \emph{teṇe kīḍī kacḍī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{કચડવું}} (\emph{kacaḍvũ}) probably belongs with \emph{kacarvũ}, \textquotedblleft{}to press\textquotedblright{}, which CDIAL sets under \emph{*kacc}, \textquotedblleft{}crush, press\textquotedblright{}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 2611). A wheel that goes over something \textbf{\gu{કચડી} \gu{નાખે} \gu{છે}}, crushes it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for careless, then the Gujarati for a fine, then say \emph{kacaḍvũ} again
\end{itemize}
